dossier.architecture: Protected pickup and short transfer into a pivoting shooter; winch climb and trap developed later.

subsystems.drivetrain: SDS MK4i: Kraken drive, Falcon steering.
subsystems.intake: Under-bumper intake; carbon rollers replaced early polycarbonate; spare assembly rebuilt after impact damage.
subsystems.transfer: Curved guides and powered roller replace slower, note-damaging conveyor concepts.
subsystems.scoring: Top/bottom launcher with increasingly stiff pivot support and external position sensing.
subsystems.endgame: Winch hooks, compliant guides and later stabilizer/trap-door work; early shooter-as-climber proposal was superseded.
subsystems.controls: Choreo/PathPlanner, characterization, procedural autos, state-machine logs and added See3CAM before DCMP.

versions: March: damper added to reduce settling; pivot ratio and belts changed before DCMP. Worlds logs diagnosed belt skipping. GRITS intake damage required emergency structural support.
dossier.analysis: Especially valuable PCH chronology: mechanical settling time was a cycle-time bottleneck; logs distinguished encoder disagreement from a simple aiming-tuning problem. The mic'd match is operational evidence, not a technical walkthrough.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.
Prior w0AFxJFMOqg link is match/driver audio, not a technical interview; construction uses team build thread 452466.

context_documents.title: 2024-2974 · Pivot-settle delay and belt skipping require dated evidence
context_documents.body:
# 2024-2974: Pivot-settle delay and belt skipping require dated evidence

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The build thread records replacing a slower, note-damaging conveyor with a more direct curved feed, carbon-roller shooter changes, replaceable intake assemblies and pivot stiffening. Later posts describe a friction damper, changing pivot belts, a ratio change from 125:1 to 100:1, and Worlds logs exposing belt skipping when the arm extended.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly ties the direct feed to speed/note preservation, the damper to waiting several seconds for the angle to settle, and the revised ratio to faster rotation. Log comparison between motor and external encoder exposed a mechanical slip rather than merely a software aiming error.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

This history explains why commanded angle, measured motor angle and true launcher angle are different quantities. Increasing control gains cannot reliably fix a slipping transmission. The fastest pivot also is not the one with the shortest complete aim-to-shot time if it oscillates afterward. The early proposal to climb using the shooter must remain a proposal unless later installation evidence supports it.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Compare motor and external encoder trajectories under arm extension, measure request-to-exit latency, and inspect intake damage after contact.

## Limits

First-party build posts in topic 452466, especially 2, 5, 21, 27 and 32. The previously linked w0AFxJFMOqg video is match/driver audio, not a technical interview; it is rejected as construction evidence here.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/452466](https://www.chiefdelphi.com/t/452466)
- [https://youtu.be/w0AFxJFMOqg](https://youtu.be/w0AFxJFMOqg)

source_reviews.title: 2974 Walton Robotics Build Blog 2024
source_reviews.review_basis: Read dated primary build and programming posts from web rendering and public topic JSON.
facts: Compared protected intake against two concepts; curved transfer replaced a longer prototype that was slow and damaged notes. Shooter design, sensor staging, intake repairs and belt diagnosis are dated separately.
source_reviews.limitations: Some posts describe proposals or practice configurations. The linked CAD, engineering summary, videos and code were not inspected for this entry.

source_reviews.title: Walton final programming update
source_reviews.review_basis: Read team account of the Worlds diagnostic and plotted signals as described in the post.
facts: Amp aiming problem was traced to divergence between pivot motor and CANCoder position during extension. The team identified belt skipping and tightened the belt.
source_reviews.limitations: Narrative evidence gives the failure and intervention. It gives no load threshold or independent durability test.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Shosty is a compact ground-to-shooter machine on MK4i modules with Kraken drive and Falcon steering. A wide protected intake passes notes into a short curved transfer rather than carrying them through a long intermediate belt path. A variable-angle top/bottom shooter covers Speaker and Amp, making the pivot part of both delivery modes. A modular winch and Trap door opener were later priorities. The most instructive tradeoff is visible in the chronology: closing the gaps between mechanisms improved handling while also making the conveyor drive and lower pivot axle harder to reach.
source_review.piece_flow: The wide floor collector hands the note into a curved guide and an active transfer roller. The team added an upstream optical sensor and a beam break at the shooter. The reported state machine brings the note to the shooter beam, then backs it off until the beam clears to avoid premature wheel contact. Ready states coordinate motor activity with sensor transitions. The team tested Speaker and Amp shots from the same launcher, reporting that waiting for spin-up made Amp delivery more consistent. Trap testing also used the shooter, with a separate mechanism proposed to open and hold the door.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Electronics were split around the central bellypan because the low-angle launcher passed over the available equipment height. Hard stops above the battery were added or planned to limit downward travel to 22.5 degrees. The camera bracket later replaced crossbars between the upper flywheel sets, turning camera mounting into a structural interface. The winch module encountered the protruding mini PC and later the main electrical panel during fit and service work.

subsystems.name: Protected intake and transfer
subsystems.construction: Carbon-fiber rollers with end adapters, 1/4-inch polycarbonate side plates and later replaceable guide pieces. Curved guide and dedicated NEO-powered upper conveyor roller.
subsystems.operation: The roller captures off-center notes and the driven curved transfer lifts the note into the shooter throat.
subsystems.team_rationale: Wide capture let drivers collect without slowing for precise alignment. The longer PVC/tubing conveyor was slower and marked notes in prototyping.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A short handoff reduces residence time but amplifies interference between the roller drive, guide supports and launcher cross members.
subsystems.interfaces: An added shooter brace collided with the earlier power-transfer belt path, so the team installed a dedicated conveyor motor above the intake. The cover above the front assembly protected the path from notes and wheel contact.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: A crowned pulley free-spun as the polybelt overheated; timing drive and additional axle support replaced it. Keep a complete spare intake and inspect bent frame stock, side plates and bumper brackets after contact.
subsystems.unknowns: Final roller gap under impact and event-specific guide dimensions.

subsystems.name: Shooter, pivot and sensing
subsystems.construction: Carbon-roller top/bottom shooter with grip treatment and guides; pivot transmission with external CANCoder, hard stops and a friction damper added around the lower axle.
subsystems.operation: The sensors stage the note out of the accelerating nip; wheel spin-up and physical pivot settling precede feeding. Team later logged request-to-exit time.
subsystems.team_rationale: The first flywheel layout lacked desired velocity. A tread-loaded damper reduced the seconds spent waiting for the pivot to settle. The 125:1 to 100:1 ratio change targeted faster motion.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: A high-resolution motor trace is only an indirect angle estimate when compliant transmission stages can slip. Compare it with the output sensor while loaded.
subsystems.interfaces: The shooter base, bottom transfer roller, front swerve modules and pivot shaft occupy intersecting service paths. Access holes reduced the amount of hardware removed to extract the lower axle.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check belt tension at both sides, matching stop heights and encoder agreement. Noisy bearings were found during a District Championship ops check.
subsystems.unknowns: Final loaded-angle repeatability, full current draw, and exact World Championship shot calibration.

subsystems.name: Winch and Trap development
subsystems.construction: Team built a winch module and reported changing hook guides and materials in development. A shooter-mounted two-pivot door opener with rotary servo release was reported in April testing.
subsystems.operation: The winch was tested on the defense base. Door-opening tests subsequently used a fully climbed, stabilized setup to obtain initial shot angles.
subsystems.team_rationale: Planar polycarbonate guides were selected to stabilize hook travel relative to rods; a second door pivot provided needed reach.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Loaded suspension pose determines the door contact location and release angle. Bench-stabilized shots omit swing and chain compliance.
subsystems.interfaces: Mini PC and panel clearance affect installation of the winch; Trap requires door pressure, stable chassis pose and a viable shooter angle at once.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect hook support material, module insertion clearance and release function as separate checks.
subsystems.unknowns: Exact event installation and competitive Trap outcomes remain open.

revisions: January concepts and February builds precede the March timing-belt transfer fix. Anderson damage motivated a spare intake and tougher guide. Post-Carrollton pivot work changed belt family and reduction; Worlds logs still caught a belt skip. GRITS later exposed a full intake side-plate crack.
transferable_principles: Record both motor-side and output-side angle while testing a loaded mechanism.
Measure request-to-exit latency when changing ratio, damping or staging.
disconfirming_conditions: If higher pivot speed produces longer settling, raw speed does not shorten the scoring cycle.
If the front structure moves under contact, nominal note clearance and spare-part interchangeability need retesting.
remaining_gaps: The separate match/audio link was excluded from construction evidence. Trap event configuration and success need primary confirmation.
